# PR #4200: Patch: a test holds the AI's per-attack combat math to the game's combat forecast on boards from seeded games, and a blow a First Strike defender stops is worth nothing to the AI

Closes #4171

## What changed

**The fix (`crates/ai/src/reply.rs`, `fight`).** The AI's model of its opponent (`fight` and `trade_value`) mishandled an attacker that a First Strike defender destroys before it can strike. It already knew such an attacker lands nothing, but `fight`'s `out` still held the blow as if it had landed. So `trade_value` still added the chip per point dealt and the Divine Shield pop. `fight` now treats such a blow as no blow at all.

It also does the same for the reverse case: the strike back that a First Strike attacker pre-empts by destroying its target first now reads as no strike back. Before, `taken` still counted it. That is how the engine's `combat_forecast` shows both cases. `kills`, `dies` and `lands` come out exactly as before; only `out` and `back` change, and only in those two cases.

In `trade_value` the only terms that change are the chip and the pop. The conversion, Lifesteal, Cleave and Trample terms were already gated on the same conditions.

**Tests.**
- **`reply.rs`, `r4171000_a_blow_a_first_strike_defender_stops_earns_no_chip_and_no_shield_pop` (new):** a 4/4 Mr. Vanilla attacks a plain Pointmaster (6/1, First Strike), and a 1/2 Oomen attacks a Radiant Pointmaster (12/2, First Strike, Divine Shield). In both cases the attack lands nothing, deals 0, pops nothing, and `trade_value` equals minus the attacker's `kill_worth`.
- **`reply.rs`, `an_attacker_a_first_strike_defender_destroys_first_heals_nothing` (corrected):** this existing test asserted the bug, a `chip_per_damage × 1` credit for a blow that never lands. Its expected value is now just the attacker lost. This corrects a wrong expectation; it does not weaken the check. Its const comment also wrongly called Pointmaster a 7/1; the catalog says 6/1 Rush, First Strike.
- **`candidates.rs`, `r4171000_the_trade_reads_agree_with_the_combat_forecast_on_seeded_games` (new):**
  - It plays `FORECAST_AGREEMENT_GAMES` (16) games of the random policy through `play_match`, both decks dealt by `build_ai_deck` from every set.
  - It collects every state through `MatchHooks.after_action`.
  - On each state it takes every Unit-target entry of either seat's `combat_forecast`, and compares `(dealt, taken, kills, survives, pops, kills_and_survives)` from `fight` and `kills_and_survives` against the forecast. `dealt` is capped at the target's health for a Trample hit (§4.4 step 5).
  - A mismatch names the seed, the action index, both cards (instance id, def id, Radiant or not), both tuples, and the counts so far.
  - Floors, each reported with all three counts when it fails: at least 1000 attacks judged, 150 distinct cards met, and 5 stopped blows (blows a First Strike defender stopped that would otherwise deal damage or pop a shield).
  - It is not `#[ignore]`d, so it runs in the per-PR `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`.

**Spec and docs.** New ruling `spec/rulings/R4171000.md` (with its **Gate.** line) and its paragraph in `spec/pending/4171.md`. One sentence added to §9.9's "The opponent's reply" in `spec/09-architecture.md`, and one clause to the reply paragraph in `crates/ai/README.md`.

**Exceptions:** none. On this branch the agreement test finds no mismatch beyond the two fixed above. `blow` and `kills_and_survives` needed no change.

## How I tested it

- `cargo test -p jackioh-ai --lib -- r4171000 an_attacker_a_first_strike`: 3 passed. The agreement test judged **2064 attacks over 246 distinct cards, with 80 stopped blows**.
- **Runtime:** the lib test binary finished in **5.02 s** (debug build), and the agreement test is nearly all of that.
- **Reverting the fix:**
  - With `main`'s `fight` put back, all three tests fail. The agreement test fails first on a pre-empted strike back: `forecast-agreement:1`, after action 59, `core-011` into `stinkyscape-t-drone-interceptor`, taken 2 vs 0.
  - With only the stopped blow left unfixed, the agreement test fails on `forecast-agreement:5`, after action 75, `meditative-031` into a plain Pointmaster (`core-020`): `left: (7, 6, false, false, false, false)`, `right: (0, 6, false, false, false, false)`.
  - The fix was restored afterwards.
- **224 seeds**, by temporarily setting the game count to 224 (since put back): 0 mismatches, 31257 attacks, 1061 cards, 411 stopped blows, 67.24 s.
- **Pool probe** (`--features jackioh-engine/pool-probe`, 16 games): passes with 2117 attacks, 224 cards and 12 stopped blows, so all three floors still hold.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`: all pass (lib 60, `ai` 937, `ai_slow` 95 with 15 daily-ignored).
- `cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo fmt --check`: exit 0.
- `cargo jackioh spec check`: `2244 rulings, 5689 proofs, 71149 citations in 4584 files, 30283 links: ok`.
- `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims`: `classify: Internal`, no problems. No patch fragment is needed, since an AI change claims no card.
- `cargo jackioh gate` (smoke): ai-vs-random 19 of 20 (17 needed), ai-vs-greedy 16 (10), hard-vs-easy 16 (16), 0 search panics.
- **Crates that depend on the AI**, run because the fix can change AI decisions: `cargo test -p jackioh-shared -p jackioh-server -p jackioh-tools -p jackioh-wasm --features jackioh-engine/testkit,jackioh-engine/ts`. All pass (server 1848 + store 747, shared, tools 572 + acceptance + golden, wasm), and `apps/web/src/wire` is unchanged.

## Decisions the issue did not settle

- **The fix is in `fight`, not `trade_value`** (the issue proposed `trade_value`). Gating chip and pop only in `trade_value` would leave `fight.out` reading as landed, so the agreement test would still pass with the fix reverted.
- **The test also compares `taken`, and the strike-back fix rides along.** Comparing all five fields surfaced the pre-empted strike back as a second mismatch of the same kind, and it is fixed in the same three lines.
- **The game count and floors are constants in the test module, not in `config.rs`.** They are test sizes, not numbers the AI plays by (rule 9 covers the latter).
- **16 games, not 24.** The floors sit at about half of what was measured and hold under the pool probe.
- **States are not filtered by phase or prompt.** `combat_forecast` lists only what `legal_actions` allows, so a state where no attack may be declared has no entries to compare.
- **The forecast's fields are not normalised in the test.** That would restate §4.3 inside a test meant to hold the AI to the engine.

## Worth a second look

- **The corrected existing test.** It encoded the bug; with the fix reverted it fails, as it should.
- **hard-vs-easy hit its smoke floor exactly (16 of 16 needed).** The fix changes how the opponent model prices attacks into a First Strike defender, so AI decisions there can change. This is a correctness fix, not a measured strength gain.
- **Floor drift.** New cards change what every seed deals. If a floor ever fails, raise `FORECAST_AGREEMENT_GAMES` rather than lowering the floor.

# #4171: Patch: a test holds the AI's per-attack combat math to the game's combat forecast on boards from seeded games, and a blow a First Strike defender stops is worth nothing to the AI
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

To plan quickly, the computer opponent works out fights with its own arithmetic instead of asking the game. The game has its own forecast of each fight, the one players are shown. Every time the two have disagreed, someone found it by reading code and fixed it by hand, about six times in the last month.

This adds a test that plays a few dozen quick random games. Whenever an attack could be made, it checks that the AI's arithmetic and the game's forecast agree about every possible attack: the damage each side deals, who dies, and whether a shield pops.

It also fixes the first disagreement already found. When a First Strike defender such as Radiant Pointmaster kills the attacker before it can strike, the AI's model of you still credits that attack with chip damage and a popped Divine Shield. So it expects you to make attacks that gain you nothing. The next disagreement a new card brings in will fail a test instead of waiting for someone to spot it.

## Why

- **The AI restates the forecast.** Its per-attack reads re-derive what the engine's `combat_forecast` and `forecast_attack` compute through `project_hit` (`crates/engine/src/query.rs:1022`, `:1059-1121`). The reads are `fight` (`crates/ai/src/reply.rs:86-117`), and `blow` and `kills_and_survives` (`crates/ai/src/candidates.rs:170-378`). Each one redoes Divine Shield, Armor and Pierce, the caps, conversion, damage pools, Poisonous and exile, First Strike order, and Ranged.
- **Each new mechanic has reached the two separately**, and they were reconciled by hand: #4064 (#4102, pools and the Burn and Toxic Rounds), #4023 (#4052, Anime Armor's cap), #4065 (#4101, The Banisher's exile, which the forecast got separately in #4151), #3937 (#4031) and #3909 (#3930).
- **The tests that hold them together compare too little.** They are `r2179005_the_trade_reads_agree_with_the_combat_forecast` (`candidates.rs:1405`, 13×13 hand-built bodies) and `r4064000_r4064001_…` (`candidates.rs:1774`, 9×9 bodies under 4 pool settings). Both compare only the kill and the death. Their bodies have no Trample, Cleave, lane multiplier or combat bonus, and neither test checks what each side deals or whether a shield pops.
- **That is how this mismatch got past them.** When a First Strike defender destroys the attacker first, `fight` sets `lands` false but leaves `out` as if the blow had landed (`reply.rs:91, 106`). `trade_value` then still adds `AI_REPLY.chip_per_damage` per point and `AI_EVAL.keyword.divine_shield` for the pop (`reply.rs:220-227`). The Lifesteal and conversion terms just below are gated on `lands`; these two are not. The forecast deals 0 and pops nothing in that case (`query.rs:1087-1091, 1118`).
- **A concrete case.** With Radiant Pointmaster (Core #20: 12/2, Rush, First Strike, Divine Shield) on the AI's field, the opponent model reads a small attacker's suicide into it as worth a shield the attacker never touches.
- **Nothing holds the AI to the forecast on real boards.** #4151 holds the forecast to the real combat for every attack played, but the AI's reads are checked only on the hand-built bodies above.

## Proposal

1. In `trade_value`, a blow that does not land (`!lands`) earns no chip and no shield pop, as the forecast reads it.
2. Add a test in the crate's unit tests, beside the two agreement tests, since `fight` is `pub(crate)`:
   - It plays `FORECAST_AGREEMENT_GAMES` seeded games of SPEC §10.7's random policy through `play_match`, with `MatchHooks.after_action` collecting each state. Both decks are dealt by `build_ai_deck` from every set.
   - On every state where a seat may attack (its Main phase, no prompt open), it takes each Unit-target entry of `combat_forecast(state, seat)`. It compares `fight` and `kills_and_survives`, under `AI_EVAL`, field by field: what the attacker deals (capped by Trample, and nothing when the blow does not land), what it takes, kills, survives, pops.
   - A mismatch fails the test, naming the seed, the action index, both cards (id and face) and each read's values.
3. The test asserts a floor on the attacks it judged and on the distinct Unit cards it met, so it cannot pass by checking nothing. It runs in the per-PR `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`.
4. Each further mismatch the test finds is fixed in the AI's read in the same PR. One that needs a rules decision too big for that PR stays a named exception in the test, with its reason, and is listed in the PR.

## Where it lands

- `crates/ai/src/reply.rs` (`fight`, `trade_value`)
- `crates/ai/src/candidates.rs` (`blow`, `kills_and_survives`, and the test module the agreement tests live in)
- Read only: `crates/ai/src/match_.rs` (`play_match`, `MatchHooks`) and `crates/engine/src/query.rs` (`combat_forecast`)
- `crates/ai/README.md` (the reply paragraph), SPEC §9.9 (The opponent's reply), a new ruling note and its paragraph in `spec/pending/<issue>.md`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A unit test: an attacker without First Strike attacks a First Strike, Divine Shield defender that destroys it first, and `trade_value` gives it no chip and no shield pop. This test fails on `main`.
- [ ] The agreement test compares all five fields on every Unit-target forecast entry of every state it collects.
- [ ] With the fix reverted, the agreement test fails: its seeds include a First Strike defender destroying an attacker first.
- [ ] It asserts its floors (attacks judged, distinct Unit cards met) and reports both counts when it fails.
- [ ] It runs per PR, not under `#[ignore]`, in a few seconds, and the PR states how long it takes.
- [ ] Any exception is named in the test with its reason and listed in the PR.
- [ ] These all pass: `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo jackioh spec check` and `cargo jackioh gate` (smoke).

## Size and risks

Medium: one small fix, a test of about 100 to 150 lines, the ruling and the docs.

The test may find more mismatches than the one above. Each should be a small fix like the six before it, but several at once make the PR larger.

Random-policy boards rarely show Radiant faces or rare keywords. The floors keep the test honest about how much it checks, but they do not promise every card, so the hand-built bodies stay.

The fix slightly changes which attacks the AI's model of the opponent expects when a First Strike defender stands, so AI decisions there can change. It is a correctness fix, not a measured strength gain.

                           met.insert(target.def_id.clone());

                                forecast's; {judged} attacks judged, {} cards met so far",
